proposed_english: becomes light / comes to ease (of body)
rationale: Two attestations on this page (lines 1 and 24) describing the comfortable bodily state in opposition to ⲧⲱⲗⲉ ⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ 'weighs upon me' (line 18). Likely Lyc variants of a single verb of bodily lightness/ease. ⲁⲥⲓⲱⲩ may be from ⲁⲥⲁⲓ̈ 'become light'; ⲁⲥⲓⲱⲣ remains uncertain — possibly the same root with -ⲣ ending, or a related verb.

ⲡⲁ- ('my') + ⲕⲉ- ('other') + ⲥⲱⲙⲁ ('body'). Manichaean technical term distinguishing the inner/spiritual body from the fleshly body. Recurs lines 1, 18 in the alternation between peaceful and disturbed states — the 'other body' is the experiential register being described.

ⲧⲁ- ('my') + ϯⲣⲭⲏ (Greek ἀρχή with prosthetic ϯ-, or article+ⲁⲣⲭⲏ). Manichaean technical term for the highest inner ruling principle, paired here with the 'other body' as the soul-faculty that rejoices in Wisdom. Retained as 'Arche' to preserve technical Greek register.
From verbal root ⲱⲕⲙ̄ 'be sad, grieved' (Crum). Substantival. ⲡⲱⲕⲙⲉ ⲣ̄ⲍⲟⲩⲟ 'the grief abounds.' Distinct from ⲗⲩⲡⲏ (Greek loan, used in same passage line 4) which is more general 'sorrow.'
Lycopolitan reflex of ϣⲛ̄-ϭⲟⲙ 'find power, be able.' The reduced ⲟⲛ- for ϣⲛ̄- and ⲑⲁⲙ for ϭⲟⲙ are dialectal features. Used in negative habitual ⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲟⲛⲑⲁⲙ 'I do not have power.'
Habitual 1sg ϣⲁⲓ̈- + ϣⲧⲣ̄ⲧⲣ̄ 'be disturbed, troubled' (already in glossary). Recurs lines 3 and 15 of this page as the diagnostic verb of the disturbed state.

proposed_english: thrust them in / drive them inward
rationale: Reduplicated form of ϣⲱⲗ 'thrust, drive' with 3pl object suffix. The reduplication intensifies the action of forceful insertion. Used line 11 of how the alien thoughts are 'thrust inward into me.'
ⲥⲣϥ̄ⲣⲁϩⲧ reduplicated qualitative on ⲥⲣϥ̄- 'be loose, idle' (cf. ⲥⲗⲱϥⲗⲉϥ 'flabby'). Diagnostic phrase for disturbed speech: the words come slack, disjointed, lacking firm articulation.

Reduplicated form possibly combining ϣⲧⲣ̄ⲧⲣ̄ 'disturb' with -ⲡⲧⲓⲡ (perhaps from ⲡⲱⲧⲡ̄ 'soft, weak' or ⲧⲏⲡⲉ 'joint'). Tentative rendering 'be undone/overthrown' — captures the body's collapse under disturbance. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

proposed_english: be at hand for / stand ready to
rationale: ⲍⲁⲗⲟ likely Lyc reflex of ϩⲁⲗⲟ/ⲱϩⲉ 'be set, stand' + ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲟⲧ 'in my hand.' Idiomatic 'is at my disposal/is ready to my hand' — used line 21 of Wisdom standing ready to assist the speaker in the proclamation.
In construction ⲙⲁⲓ̈ⲥⲓⲭⲁⲛⲉ 'I do not habitually weary' (line 24). Possibly Lyc form of a weariness/cessation verb. Could alternatively be 'be silent.' Confidence low.

ⲡⲁ- + ϫⲓⲛ-. ϫⲓⲛ likely the Coptic nominalizing prefix substantivized = 'manner, mode, way.' ⲡⲁϫⲓⲛ ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'my whole way' (line 5) — the totality of the speaker's mode of existence. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

Two attestations (lines 9, 26) in the construction 'on/in this ⲡⲉⲓⲗⲁⲏ.' Likely Lyc reflex of ⲗⲁϩ 'occasion, time, circumstance' (cf. ⲗⲁⲁⲉⲍ 'occasion' in glossary). Functions as temporal-circumstantial pronoun 'on this occasion.'
Perfect 1sg ⲉⲧⲁⲓ̈- + ϫⲛⲟⲩ 'ask, inquire' + 3pl object -ⲟⲩ. Standard Coptic verb of formal inquiry. Used line 28 of the disciple's two-part question to the Apostle.

Greek loanword αἰσθάνεσθαι 'perceive by the senses' with Coptic verbal prefix ⲣ̄-. Used line 29 'I do not perceive' — the disciple's failure of sensory-cognitive grasp of the matter producing his alternating states.
